subject: Financial Management and Strategic Management
paper_name: Paper-6: Financial Management and Strategic Management
question_text:
(b)  B Ltd. has received an offer to get a discount of 2% on an invoice value of
`75,000, if payment is made within one month instead of normal credit terms
of 3 months. If the company makes early payment, it will need to finance the
payment through a bank overdraft of 10% p.a. Tax rate is 30%.

Whether B Ltd. should accept the offer? Support your decision with
calculations.
(3 Marks)
suggested_answer:
(b) Discount on early payment = 2% x 75,000 = `1,500

Net Benefit (A)
= ` 1,500 - Tax (30%) = ` 1,050

The company must borrow the discounted invoice amount via a bank
overdraft for the 2-month period.

Amount to be Borrowed = 75,000 − 1,500 = ` 73,500

Bank overdraft interest for 2 months:

= P × R × T
= 73,500 × 10% × 2/12

= ` 1,225

After tax interest cost  = 1,225 × (1−0.30)
= 1,225 × 0.70
= ` 857.50

Net Saving

= Net Benefit – Net Interest Cost

= ` 1,050 – ` 857.50

= ` 192.50 (Net Saving)

Since the company gains a net benefit of ` 192.50 by making early payment,
B Ltd. should accept the discount offer.

Alternatively, the question can be solved as below:

Annualized benefit of discount

=
Discount %
12 months
×
100-Discount %
Credit Period – Discount Period

= 2/98 x 12/2 x 100
=12.245 %

Post tax benefit
= 12.245 x (1-0.3) =8.571

Post tax Bank OD rate
= 10% x (1-0.3) =7%

Benefit of discount is more than cost of OD. Hence, discount should be
accepted.
